name: Fast, short-lived colony on dung or compost
description: Thin, fast, unbundled hyphae form a dense radial colony on a rich, short-lived substrate such as dung, compost or freshly burnt soil. The colony fruits quickly and then dies back; it does not form cords and loses to competitors once they arrive.

tip_speed.note: placeholder carried over from the type species Coprinopsis cinerea, for which no rate was found; ruderal colonies are put at 5 to 20 mm/day (210 to 830 um/h) in research/02 section 4

branch_angle.note: from the type species Coprinopsis cinerea: dikaryon branches at 10 to 45 degrees (research/01-growth-biology.md [7])

branch_angle_sd.note: as for the type species Coprinopsis cinerea: default from Hopkins & Boswell 2012 (79 +/- 10 deg, research/09); not measured for the type species

sensitivity.note: how strongly tips turn away from crowding; model coefficient

fusion_probability.note: chance a tip that meets a hypha fuses and does not cross; no measurement found

density_cap.note: hyphal density at which branching stops; tuning value

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / segment length so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found

inactivation_rate.note: as for the type species Coprinopsis cinerea: from Rhizoctonia solani (Boswell et al. 2003, research/09); not this species (0.5 per day)

degradation_rate.note: none seen in 15 h in R. solani; small value so dead hyphae clear

passive_transport.note: diffusion between neighbouring segments; measured diffusion inside hyphae (1 to 2 x 10^-9 m2/s, research/10) is several times faster than the passes allow

soil.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from its ecology, not measured

wood.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from its ecology, not measured

litter.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from its ecology, not measured

root.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from its ecology, not measured

agar.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from its ecology, not measured

transport_speed.note: as for the type species Coprinopsis cinerea: no measurement for the type species; near the 14.4 mm/h ceiling for motor transport and the 18 mm/h mass flow measured in Neurospora (research/10)

t_opt.note: typical optimum near 28 C across 37 wood-decay isolates (research/06 [3]); not measured for this family. The type species Coprinopsis cinerea grows best at 37 C (research/08 [17]), which is unusual and is kept in its own file

cold_drop.note: cultivated basidiomycetes commonly need a downshift of 5 to 10 C (research/05 [2][5]); low end used. The type species needs 9 C

min_age.note: as for the type species Coprinopsis cinerea: initial to mushroom takes 4 to 5 days and the whole cycle about two weeks (research/01 [7])

wobble.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

avoidance.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

fusion_probability.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

uptake.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

turn.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

spike_interval.note: default; no recording for any member of this family (research/04)

spike_duration.note: default; no recording for any member of this family (research/04)

spike_amplitude.note: default; no recording for any member of this family (research/04)

score.note: ruderal first arrivals are treated like primary colonisers, the lowest rank in the wood-decay hierarchy (research/06 section 2.5 [4]); Pyronema is noted to lose to competitors once soil life returns (research/08). Not measured for this family
